newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian tax reform summit to start Friday.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian tax reform summit to start Friday.

text.p: About 200 Australian business and community representatives will meet here on Friday to discuss improvements to the country's tax system.

The National Tax Reform Summit, convened by the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ACCI) and the Australian Council of Social Service (ACOSS), was aimed at promoting informed debate about tax reform involving the entire community.
"The trouble with the debate about tax reform in this country is that people don't properly understand the issues," the ACCI and ACOSS said in a joint statement.
"If we're going to have a debate about tax reform, all aspects of the tax system need to be included in the discussion.
"This is the first time we have come together as a community to discuss these issues and give people an opportunity to develop a broader understanding of the diversity of views."
However, the ACCI and ACOSS said it was unlikely the summit would consider a specific set of reform proposals, nor was it likely to lead to the development of a tax package.
"But it is the start of the process and we are hopeful that some areas of commonality and agreement on broad principles will emerge to move the tax debate forward," they said.
They said both businesses and community sectors wanted a tax system which minimised tax avoidance and evasion as well as the cost of tax collection.
However, both sectors recognised that tax reform should lead to sustainable economic and employment growth through enhanced savings, while generating adequate government revenue.

Summit participants included the Motor Trades Association of Australia, the Real Estate Institute of Australia, the Australian Bankers Association, and accountants Ernst & Young, KPMG Peat Marwick and Deloitte Touche Tomatsu.
